summary: The video, priority, sprite and audio-mixing logic is organized around MAME's darius.cpp and pc080sn.cpp rather than the board. Tile layers are composited in MAME's update_screen order and tagged with MAME's priority-bitmap values (1/2), and a GFX_PMASK_2-style test decides sprite-over-layer. The sprite engine walks sprite RAM using draw_sprites' own expressions, including the 'curx > 900' wrap constant. The audio mixer reimplements MAME's software pan/volume model ((pan*vol)>>8 against a 0..100 dB-curve table). The bus decode reproduces MAME handler quirks such as cpua_ctrl_w's byte-swap heuristic. Nothing is expressed as board nets, PALs, PROMs or raster-counter-driven fetch timing, and the video timing is an invented 1527x262 raster.

findings.signal: MAME priority-bitmap values and primask in compositor
findings.note: Tile pixels are tagged prio 2'b01 for layer 0 and 2'b10 for layer 1, which are MAME's screen.priority() values from the two tilemap_draw_offset calls. The final mux lets a sprite through when (sprite_prio[0] || tile_prio != 2'b10), which reproduces MAME's GFX_PMASK_2 / 0 primask table rather than a board priority PROM or gate network.

findings.signal: layer draw order reproduced in one batch buffer
findings.note: One state machine first writes layer 0 into the line buffer unconditionally (TILEMAP_DRAW_OPAQUE), then rewinds prep_out_x and overdraws layer 1 only where the pixel is non-zero (transparent pen 0). That is MAME's sequential draw order, not two PC080SN layer outputs mixed per pixel.

The scan FSM steps through each 4-word sprite entry and reuses MAME's expressions: sy = (256 - word0) & 0x1ff, sx = word1 & 0x3ff minus x_offs with 'if (sx > 900) sx -= 1024', code = word2 & 0x1fff with flip bits 14/15, color = word3 & 0x7f, prio = bit 7, skip if code == 0. The 900/1024 wrap is MAME's software clip heuristic. Hardware would wrap on its counter width.

cpua_ctrl_data takes the high byte when (data[15:8] != 0 && data[7:0] == 0). That is the line 'if ((data & 0xff00) && ((data & 0xff) == 0)) data >>= 8' from MAME's handler, a software workaround with no evident latch equivalent on the board.

Volume nibbles from the YM2203 I/O ports go through a 16-entry 0..100 lookup (a dB curve shaped like MAME's m_def_vol, with values close to but not equal to MAME's), and each channel gain is (pan*vol)>>8 and ((255-pan)*vol)>>8. The nibble-to-channel assignment matches MAME's m_vol[] indexing exactly. The core recreates MAME's filter_volume gain calculation instead of modelling the board's analog volume/pan circuitry.

Each MAME map line becomes its own full-range comparator (sel_c00060, sel_d40000, ...) with a matching per-entry ENABLE_* parameter. coin_word is written at C00060 and read back at C0000E, and it gates the coin bits, following MAME's m_coin_word model. The decode is not written as board address-line decoders or PALs.

findings.signal: three panels as MAME xoffs instances
findings.note: The three PC080SN panels are one parameterized renderer instantiated with X_OFFSET 0/288/576, added to the source x. All three share one VRAM, and only the left instance owns the scroll registers. This follows MAME's single double-width pc080sn device rendered three times with an x offset, not three chips with their own pins.

findings.mame_ref: taito/darius.cpp:darius() screen config (60 Hz, 36*8 x 32*8, irq4_line_hold)
findings.note: The raster is a synthetic 864+663 x 262 counter at 24 MHz, and IRQ4 is a pending bit set on render_y >= 224 and cleared on IACK (MAME's irq4_line_hold). No H/V counter bits drive fetch phases, and no board sync or blank equations appear.

findings.signal: PC060HA as its own chip module
findings.note: The sound communication chip is a standalone module with master and slave port/comm ports, 4-bit pointer registers, a nibble-wide 8-entry shared RAM and NMI/reset outputs, processed on CS falling edges. Its granularity matches the custom chip, though the same split also exists as a MAME device, so the signal is weak.

Scroll and flip control are latched at the start of each line, whereas MAME applies them once per frame. This is closer to how a scanning chip behaves, but it is also a natural consequence of a line-buffer design, so it is weak evidence.

findings.signal: sprite RAM scanned in reverse order
findings.note: Sprites are scanned from max_idx_used down to 0, with last write winning, so entry 0 ends up on top. MAME goes in ascending order. The core diverges here, but nothing in the code shows the order comes from hardware, so it is counted neither way.
Attributes come from VRAM 0x0000-0x3fff and codes from 0x4000-0x7fff, with flip in bits 14/15 and FG code & 0x7ff / color & 0x7f. Any correct core must share this data layout with MAME.
